text: Straight up means a hundred and twenty metres under twelve carbines. Jaeha crosses it out.
Uncle Pyo knows a back door. Halfway up, a sludge outlet looks across the canyon at the rim, with nothing in between anymore.
Moon Ahin knows what he'll ask before he asks. Her husks have been a wall and a door tonight. Now, a bridge.
Her baton comes up. She isn't saying yes. She isn't saying no, either.
Borro charges up the walkway in field form, everyone packed behind his cracked shield.
Twelve carbines open up from the top, and the bolts hammer his shield.
Lyra fires back over it, arrow after arrow.
Jaeha carries both, and every bolt on that shield jolts through him.
A bolt pins Ho to the wall by his tabard. Woo rips him free. Ho is sure it was flirting.
Then Nib dives into the sludge mouth, and everyone pours in after him.
Borro backs in last, his shield taking one final volley.
Up top, Sora isn't worried. That hole ends at a cliff. She takes her squad to wait at the rim.
The sludge tunnel ends on a narrow lip of stone, high on the open canyon face.
And there it is, across forty metres of air: the gate's rim, inside Kanghan's closing iris. Five minutes twelve.
To Dami, that light is her daughter. To Ho, it's across a great deal of nothing.
Moon Ahin does the arithmetic. Thirty husks would carry everyone, and it won't be kind to them.
Jaeha doesn't push. They're hers, so it's her choice. Nobody ever gave him one about his own husks.
That surprises her more than the gap does.
She lays a hand on Number One's blank face, something she has never done. The order sounds like a plea: hold on to her.
Then she conducts with both arms, fierce and alight, and her husks leap into the air, each catching the one before.
The chain reaches the far side, and Number One locks onto the old walkway stump.
A sagging lattice of white husks spans the abyss, creaking and swaying.
Jaeha is in awe, and says so. Their owner would like him to start walking before she changes her mind.
Nib runs across first, light as a cat. Dami follows, arms out for balance.
Woo and Ho cross hand in hand. Then Borro steps on, and the bridge groans.
One husk cracks under his weight and falls away into three hundred metres of air.
Moon Ahin flinches, and the baton falters for one beat. Under her breath: twenty-nine.
Cracks spider across the husks, and Borro freezes in the middle.
Jaeha has a strange thought. Her husks are summons too, just hollow. And he carries summons.
The system agrees. All twenty-nine can be linked, and husks never refuse. Carry them?
His eyes go wide, then harden. He knows how it feels to be the thing everyone spends first.
Twenty-nine threads run into the bridge. The cracks stop, and bruises bloom up his arms instead. Two hundred and forty percent: critical.
Their summoner sees the bruises, and has to ask. His answer comes with a crooked smile: they're carrying us.
Her composure breaks, and she turns to the bridge so he won't see her eyes.
Borro moves again, and the husks hold. Nib pulls the brothers onto the ledge.
Then a side door bangs open on the ledge, and Sora's troopers pour out.
Lyra shoots the first carbine over the edge, and claims the bridge as hers.
Moon Ahin, who is conducting the actual bridge, would like to know since when. She almost smiles.
Lyra has a legal argument: her boots are on the end of it. That counts.
Nib leaps into the troopers in field form. Nobody is carrying him, so every hit is his own.
He goes through them like a gust of wind, and still pulls one back from the edge.
Borro and the crew reach the ledge, and Jaeha drops Borro's link to carry the husks. Three minutes ten.
Lyra runs the bridge, light and fast, turning mid-stride to shoot back.
The bridge only holds while she conducts, so she'll conduct as she walks. Modesty is not her talent.
They step onto the bridge together, her right arm conducting, her left holding him up.
Through his greying eyes: cracked white backs, empty air, and his blood dripping onto a husk.
A husk cracks under his foot. He stumbles, and she hauls him upright without missing a beat.
A bruise blooms across his forearm in the exact shape of the crack.
She orders him not to faint on her husks. He promises, as politely as ever.
Nib waves them on from the ledge. Behind him, the rim is narrower than a man now.
Three-quarters of the way. Two minutes four.
And while everyone watches Jaeha, a black boot steps onto Number One's back.
Han Sora stands on the end of the bridge, crossbow raised: cold, beautiful, and blocking the only way home.
She greets him like an old friend, then asks him not to move.
They stop dead. The baton freezes. Even the husks hold their breath.
Her eye along the sights is perfectly steady.
The bolt is aimed dead at the T-4 stencilled on his chest.
Jaeha smiles down the bolt, ever the polite trap-tester, and points out what she's standing on: a very brave husk.
One minute fifty-eight, a crossbow on his heart, and three hundred metres of air below.
